name: City Council Meeting - Nov 19, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  NOVEMBER 19, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  IN COUNCIL CHAMBER AT 3031 TORRANCE BL.

1.  CALL TO ORDER/ROLL CALL

2.  FLAG SALUTE/NON-SECTARIAN INVOCATION

3.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

4.  MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES
  AFTER NUMBER AND TITLE

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS

  6A. PROCLAMATION declaring November 30, 2024 through December 07, 2024 as
  Torrance Small Business Week in the City of Torrance.

  6B. City Manager and Fire – Accept and Appropriate Donation for the Community
  Emergency Response Team (CERT). Expenditure: None.

7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

  8A. Public Works – Adopt RESOLUTION Approving Program Supplement, and
  Appropriate Funds for Design of Citywide Traffic Signal Improvements, T-171.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council:
  1. Adopt a RESOLUTION approving Program Supplement No. F019 to Administering
  Agency-State Agreement for Federal Aid Projects No. 07-5249F15 for the design of the
  Citywide Traffic Signal Improvements, T-171, CRPL-5249(035); and
  2. Appropriate Carbon Reduction Program (CRP) grant funds in the amount of $88,530 to
  the Citywide Traffic Signal Improvements, T-171, thereby increasing the T-171 project
  budget from $1,793,000 to $1,881,530.

  8B. Public Works – Approve First Amendment to Goldsworthy Desalter Ground
  Lease Agreement with Water Replenishment District of Southern California
  (WRD) and Adopt RESOLUTION Determining Portion of Certain City-Owned
  Property Not Required for City Purposes and that Leasing the Property is in the
  Public Interest. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council:
  1. Approve a first amendment to the site lease agreement with the Water Replenishment
  District of Southern California (WRD) of Lakewood, CA (C2021-164) for the
  Goldsworthy Desalter at the City Services Facilities (City Yard) located at 20500
  Madrona Avenue to provide approximately 16,591 square feet of additional leased land
  for the expansion of the Goldsworthy Desalter; and
  2. Adopt a RESOLUTION determining a portion of certain City-owned property is not
  required for City purposes and that leasing the property is in the public interest.

  8C. City Manager – Adopt RESOLUTION Pursuant to Memorandum of Understanding
   (MOU) Setting Forth Hours, Wages, and Working Conditions for Torrance Police
  Commanders’ Association (TPCA). Expenditure: $971,568 (General Fund:
  Approximately $485,784 Annually).
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council adopt a RESOLUTION pursuant to
  the memorandum of understanding (MOU) setting forth the hours, wages, and working
  conditions for employees represented by the Torrance Police Commanders Association
  (TPCA) for the period beginning January 1, 2024, and ending December 31, 2025.

8D. City Clerk – SECOND AND FINAL READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 3939. Second
  and Final Reading of ORDINANCE NO. 3939 amending Chapter 11, Article 6 of
  Division 9, by amending Section 911.6.100 pertaining to Prohibited Signs;
  Repealing Article 10 – Enforcement; Adding Article 10 – Electronic/Digital
  Billboards; and Adding Article 11 – Enforcement and approve an Ordinance
  Summary for publication. This item is for consideration of adoption of the
  ordinance only. The item was previously discussed, and action was taken at a
  prior council meeting.

8E.  Public Works – Adopt Categorical Exemption Under California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) Sections 15269(a) and 15269(b) and Authorize Payment for
  Emergency Slope Repairs Between Vista Montana and Vista Largo. Expenditure:
  $424,928.66 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council:
  1. Adopt a California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Categorical Exemption, pursuant
  to Guidelines Section 15269(a) and 15269(b) for emergency slope repairs between
  Vista Montana and Vista Largo; and
  2. Authorize direct payment to Ford Foundation Drilling, Inc. of Azusa, CA in the amount
  of $378,543.66 for emergency retaining wall construction performed on Vista Montana
  in May and June 2024; and
  3. Authorize direct payment to Clarke Contracting Corporation of Lawndale, CA in the
  amount of $46,385.00 for emergency roadway repairs performed on Vista Montana in
  June and July 2024.

8F.  City Manager – Adopt Categorical Exemption Under California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) Section 15301 and Approve Fourth Amendment to Lease for
  Portion of City-Owned Property Located at 1520 Greenwood Avenue within
  Greenwood Park. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1. Adopt a California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Categorical Exemption pursuant
  to Guideline Section 15301 (Existing Facilities); and
  2. Approve a fourth amendment to Lease by and between the City of Torrance (City) and
  KinderCare Education LLC (C2000-101), to utilize a portion of City-owned property to
  continue operation of a day care facility at 1520 Greenwood Avenue within Greenwood
  Park.

8G. Public Works and General Services – Authorize Purchase Order for Six (6) 2026
  Autocar/Heil ACX64 Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Refuse Trucks as a
  Cooperative Purchase with Sourcewell. Expenditure $3,363,305.37 (Non-General
  Fund).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director and General Services Director that City
  Council authorize a purchase order with Velocity Truck Centers, LLC of Fontana, CA in the
  amount of $3,363,305.37, for six (6) 2026 Autocar/Heil ACX64 Compressed Natural Gas
  (CNG) Refuse Trucks as a cooperative purchase with Sourcewell.

8H. General Services and Fire – Appropriate Funds and Authorize Purchase Order for
  Two (2) 2024 Ford F-450 Medix Metro Express 153 Type I Ambulances as a
  Cooperative Purchase with Houston-Galveston Area Council (H-GAC).
  Expenditure: $640,976.41 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the General Services Director and Fire Chief that City Council:
  1. Appropriate $640,976.41 from the Fleet Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fund balance to
  the Fleet Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fiscal year 2024-25 operating budget; and
  2. Authorize a purchase order with Republic EVS of Huntington Beach, CA in the amount
  of $640,976.41, including sales tax, for two (2) 2024 Ford F-450 Medix Metro Express
  153 Type I ambulances as a cooperative purchase with the Houston-Galveston Area
  Council (H-GAC).
 8I.  City Manager – Approve Request to Set Closed Hearing Date to Consider
  Employee Termination Appeal. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council approve request to set a date of
  Tuesday, January 14, 2025 to conduct a closed hearing to consider an appeal of the Civil
  Service Commission’s decision sustaining the termination of a Police Officer (11).

8J.  Traffic Commission and Public Works – Accept and File Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-24
  Traffic Commission Annual Report. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Traffic Commission and Public Works Director that City Council
  accept and file the FY2023-24 Traffic Commission Annual Report.

8K. Civil Service Commission and Human Resources – Approve Examination to Fill
  Finance Director Position. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Civil Service Commission and Human Resources Director that City
  Council approve the examination to fill the position of Finance Director on an open basis.

8L.  City Treasurer – Accept and File Investment Report for the Month of September
  2024. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Treasurer that City Council accept and file the Investment
  Report for the month of September 2024.

8M. Civil Service Commission and Human Resources – Approve Reclassification of
  1.0 Full-Time Employee (FTE) Fire Battalion Chief. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Civil Service Commission and Human Resources Director that City
  Council approve the reclassification of 1.0 full-time employee (FTE) Fire Battalion Chief
  position to the classification of 1.0 FTE Deputy Fire Chief position.

8N. General Services – Adopt California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Categorical Exemption Pursuant to Section 15301 and Approve Contract
  Services Agreements for On-Call Roofing Services at Various City Facilities.
  Expenditure: $4,500,000 (General Fund: Not-to-Exceed $500,000 Annually Per
  Contract).
  Recommendation of the General Services Director that City Council:
  1. Adopt a California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Categorical Exemption pursuant
  to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities); and
  2. Approve a contract services agreement with Rainy Day Roofing, Inc of Rancho
  Cucamonga, CA in the amount of $1,500,000 for on-call roofing services for a period
  beginning November 19, 2024 and ending June 30, 2027; and
  3. Approve a contract services agreement with Bazan Roofing, Inc. of Azusa, CA in the
  amount of $1,500,000 for on-call roofing services for a period beginning November 19,
  2024 and ending June 30, 2027; and
  4. Approve a contract services agreement with Rite-Way Roofing Corp. of Fontana, CA in
  the amount of $1,500,000 for on-call roofing services for a period beginning November
  19, 2024 and ending June 30, 2027.

8O. General Services – Adopt California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Categorical Exemption Pursuant to Section 15301 and Approve Contract
  Services Agreements for On-Call Job Order Contract General Contractor
  Services Through Sourcewell. Expenditure: $4,500,000 (General Fund: Not-to-
  Exceed $750,000 Annually Per Contract).
  Recommendation of the General Services Director that City Council:
  1. Adopt a California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Categorical Exemption pursuant
  to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities); and
  2. Approve a contract services agreement with Harry H. Joh Construction, Inc of
  Paramount, CA in the amount of $2,250,000 for on-call services through Sourcewell for
  a period beginning November 19, 2024 and ending June 30, 2027; and
  3. Approve a contract services agreement with MDJ Management, LLC of El Segundo,
  CA in the amount of $2,250,000 for on-call services through Sourcewell for a period
  beginning November 19, 2024 and ending June 30, 2027.

8P.  City Clerk – Approve City Council Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council approve the City Council minutes of
  October 08, 2024, October 22, 2024 and October 29, 2024.
 9.  HEARINGS

  9A. Public Works and Water Commission - Conduct Public Hearing and Adopt
  RESOLUTION Approving Proposed Series of Annual Increases of Municipal
  Water Rates Over a Five-Year Period Beginning January 1, 2025 and Ending
  December 31, 2029.
  Recommendation of the Water Commission and Public Works Director that City Council:
  1. Conduct a public hearing on a series of annual rate increases; and
  2. Adopt a RESOLUTION approving a proposed series of annual rate increases of
  Torrance Municipal Water rates for a five-year period beginning January 1, 2025 and
  ending December 31, 2029; and
  3. Maintain the discount rate for low-income senior and disabled customers.

  9B. Community Development – Conduct Public Hearing, Adopt Categorical
  Exemption Under California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and Adopt
  Pipeline Franchise ORDINANCE Replacing Pipeline Franchise Ordinance No.
  3474 Zenith Energy West Coast Terminals LLC. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1. Conduct a Public Hearing to consider replacing expired Pipeline Franchise Ordinance
  No. 3474 with Zenith Energy West Coast Terminals LLC; and
  2. Adopt a Categorical Exemption under California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to Section 15301 (existing facilities) of the Guidelines implementing CEQA;
  and
  3. Adopt a Pipeline Franchise ORDINANCE with Zenith Energy West Coast Terminals
  LLC for a ten-year term, with one ten-year option to extend; and
  4. Approve an Ordinance Summary for Publication.

  9C. Community Development - Conduct Public Hearing on Analysis of Impediments
  to Fair Housing Choice (AI) and Approve Final AI. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1. Conduct a public hearing and take public testimony on the Analysis of Impediments to
  Fair Housing Choice (AI) covering the period July 1, 2024-June 30, 2028; and
  2. Approve Final AI.

  9D. Community Development – Conduct Public Hearing on the Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-
  24 Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) and
  Appropriate FY 2023-24 and 2024-25 Project Expenditure Budgets. Expenditure:
  None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1. Conduct a public hearing on the Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-24 Consolidated Plan Annual
  Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) to the U.S Department of Housing and
  Urban Development (HUD); and
  2. Appropriate the full amount of the FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 HOME Investment
  Partnerships Program (HOME) and Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
  awards to a newly created grant project.

10.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  10A. Finance - Accept and File Forensic Review of Financial Processes Report.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council accept and file the forensic
  review of the City’s financial processes report.

  10B. City Clerk – Discuss and Consider Amending Torrance Municipal Code
  Regarding Changes to Commission Compensation. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council:
  1. Discuss and consider amending the Torrance Municipal Code regarding changes to
  Commission Compensation; and
  2. Discuss and Consider directing the City Clerk to bring back an ORDINANCE amending
  Torrance Municipal Code Sections 13.1.1, 13.2.1, 13.3.1, 13.4.1, 13.5.1, 13.9.1,
  13.10.1, 13.11.1, 13.15.1, 13.16.1, 13.18.1, 13.20.010 and 13.21.020 all titled “Created,
  Composition, Compensation, and Qualifications”; and
  3. Determine that the project is exempt from California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
   pursuant to Sections 15378 and 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines.

  10C. Community Services – Adopt Categorical Exemption Under California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Sections 15378 and 15061(b)(3) and Discuss
  and Consider Adopting an Ordinance Amending the Torrance Municipal Code
  Pertaining to Public Art Murals and Adopt a RESOLUTION Relating to Mural
  Policy. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager, City Attorney and Community Services Director that
  City Council:
  1. Adopt a categorical exemption under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  under Sections 15378 and 15061(b)(3); and
  2. Discuss and consider adopting an ordinance amending Chapter 11 of Division 9
  entitled Signs
  3. Approve an ordinance summary for publication
  4. Adopt a RESOLUTION for the City’s mural policy.

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS

12.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS#2 (Limited up to a 15 minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comment on items that are not on the agenda. Under the
  Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on items raised during public comment
  but may respond briefly to statements made or questions posed; request clarification;
  or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral
  Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per
  speaker. If presenting handout material to Council, please provide 11 copies to the
  City Clerk before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you speak.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

  13A. The City Council will meet in Closed Session for the following purpose:
  a.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION (California Government Code
  § 54957(b)(1)): Title: City Manager
  b.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION (California
  Government Code § 54956.9(d)(1)):
  c.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code §
  54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  d.  REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code § 54956.8):
  e.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION (Initiation of
  Litigation Pursuant to California Government Code § 54956.9(d)(4)): One case.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

  14A. Adjournment of City Council meeting to Tuesday, December 3, 2024, at 5:00 p.m.
  for closed session, with regular business commencing at 6:30 p.m. in the LeRoy
  J. Jackson Council Chamber. Tuesday, November 26, 2024 is a City Council Dark
  Night.
